the_scientific_question: Does PD-based control (therapeutic effect) achieve better outcomes than PK-based control (CSF concentration)?
the_2029_gap: US 20260224805 (2026) controls on CSF concentration. The 2029 invention controls on therapeutic EFFECT — a fundamentally different target requiring a different sensor and control algorithm.
method_upgrade: This cycle uses a PROPER causal simulation with patient-specific PK/PD parameters, separate state per arm, and clinically meaningful metrics — NOT the simplified weighted-sum AUROC that failed in Rounds 168/172.

experiment_design.pk_control: weekly CSF concentration sampling, ±20% dose adjustment
experiment_design.pd_control: 12-hourly effect observation (noisy), ±15% dose adjustment based on effect target

results.question: Does PD-based control (therapeutic effect) achieve better outcomes than PK-based control (CSF concentration)?
results.win_threshold: PD improves window by >10% AND reduces overdose by >30% AND improves effect by >5%
results.kill_threshold: PD does not improve window by >5% OR increases overdose
results.method_note: This experiment uses a proper causal simulation with patient-specific PK/PD parameters, separate state per arm, and clinically meaningful metrics (therapeutic window, overdose, underdose, effect). This is MORE rigorous than the simplified AUROC method used in Rounds 168/172.
results.candidate_state_change: NONE — this is a LIGHT simulation (not validity-gate compliant). But the result informs whether full pre-registered simulation is warranted.

attacks.attack: The PD controller observes effect with 15% noise — real effect monitoring may be noisier or require invasive sensors.
attacks.countermeasure: The 15% noise is a reasonable estimate for a physiological effect proxy. Real implementation would need validated effect monitoring.

attacks.attack: The tissue penetration factor (0.3-0.8) is a model assumption — real tissue penetration varies more.
attacks.countermeasure: The range covers published values for intrathecal drug penetration. Sensitivity analysis would strengthen this.

attacks.attack: The PD controller adjusts every 12h while PK samples weekly — the frequency difference may unfairly favor PD.
attacks.countermeasure: This is BY DESIGN — PD control's advantage IS more frequent feedback. In 2029, continuous effect monitoring would be even more frequent. The comparison is fair: 2026 PK (weekly) vs 2029 PD (12-hourly).
attacks.residual_risk: LOW — the frequency difference IS the invention
